id: # Columns, the `on` grammar and driver keys: vault/architecture/guard-file-formats.md and
# vault/architecture/qg-builtin-drivers.md in the vault-quality-gates repo. Empty cells are `-`.
# Commit rows measure a copy of the staged tree through quality/bin/in-tree.sh, in a container with
# no network. Release rows run in a fresh server container on the pushed folder through
# quality/bin/in-server.sh. Whole-suite rows run on `baseline` only: the measured run takes about an
# hour, so release rows read the reports it leaves and coverage-age-days refuses a stale one.

why: replaced by format-staged-files, which counts the files Pint would change instead of reading its exit code
A commit may not stage PHP that Pint would reformat, so style changes never mix with logic changes in review.
A commit may not add a PHPStan error, so type errors never reach a release branch.

args: runner=quality/bin/in-tree.sh files=changed include=^app/ ruleset=quality/phpmd-commit.xml baseline=quality/phpmd-baseline.xml phpini=error_reporting=24575
why: A commit may not add a PHPMD clean-code, design, naming or size violation in app/ beyond quality/phpmd-baseline.xml.

args: runner=quality/bin/in-tree.sh files=changed include=^app/ exclude=^app/Models/ ruleset=quality/phpmd-commit-coupling.xml baseline=quality/phpmd-coupling-baseline.xml phpini=error_reporting=24575
why: A commit may not raise the coupling of a class in app/ outside the models beyond its baseline.
A commit may not add a coding-standard violation on the lines it adds; older lines are cleaned up on their own.
A commit may not add a suppression comment, so a finding is fixed instead of hidden.
A commit may not add entries to phpstan-baseline.neon or the PHPMD baseline, so recorded debt never absorbs a new finding.
A commit may not add entries to the PHPMD coupling baseline, so coupling debt is only paid down.
replaced by protected-paths-touched, which reads the longer protected list of quality/config
A commit may not change a protected gate file, so an agent cannot loosen the gate that judges it.

args: paths=app min-lines=10 min-tokens=70 format=php ignore=**/app/Http/Docs/** include=^app/.*\.php$ exclude=^app/Http/Docs/
why: A commit may not paste a block of ten or more lines that already exists in app/, so shared logic is extracted instead of copied.
A commit may not add a form request whose rules repeat an existing one, so each validation rule lives in one place.
A commit may not add an error under the strict PHPStan configuration beyond its baseline, so strictness only rises.
A commit may not add entries to the strict PHPStan baseline, so strict findings are fixed rather than recorded.
A commit may not add a test smell on the test lines it adds, so new tests assert behaviour instead of implementation.
replaced by format-files, which counts the files Pint would change instead of reading its exit code
A release may not ship code that Pint would reformat.
The PHP Insights code score of app/ may not drop more than half a point below its baseline.
The PHP Insights complexity score of app/ may not drop more than half a point, so methods stay small enough to follow.
The PHP Insights architecture score of app/ may not drop more than half a point, so the layering rules keep holding.
The PHP Insights style score is recorded on every release to show its trend; Pint and phpcs enforce the style itself.

args: parser=jscpd artifact=quality-reports/jscpd/jscpd-report.json#percentage -- npm_config_registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ pnpm dlx jscpd@5.3.2 app -c quality/jscpd.json --reporters json --no-colors
why: The share of duplicated lines in app/ may not rise more than 0.1 points above its baseline.
The number of duplicated blocks in app/, read from the duplication row's report, may not rise above its baseline.
replaced by phpstan-errors-all, which also counts the errors PHPStan reports without a file
The whole-repo PHPStan error count, file-less errors included, may not rise above its baseline.

args: -- mkdir -p quality-reports && { git ls-files > quality-reports/indication-tracked.txt && git diff --name-only --diff-filter=M "{{base}}...HEAD" -- database/migrations > quality-reports/indication-migrations.txt || exit 2; } && jq -n --rawfile t quality-reports/indication-tracked.txt --rawfile m quality-reports/indication-migrations.txt '{tracked_files: ($t | split("\n") | map(select(. != ""))), modified_migrations: ($m | split("\n") | map(select(. != "")))}' > quality-reports/indication-gitfacts.json && git show HEAD:quality/bin/in-server.sh | bash -s -- "$PWD" - env INDICATION_CHECKS_ROOT=/app INDICATION_CHECKS_GITFACTS=/app/quality-reports/indication-gitfacts.json sh -c 'php -n quality/indication-checks.php "$1" 2>&1' indication-checks {{base}}
why: Breaches of the project's written working rules that quality/indication-checks.php detects may not rise above their baseline.
Packages the code uses without requiring them in composer.json may not rise above their baseline.
A release may not require a package in composer.json that no code uses.
Comment lines per code line in app/ may not rise more than 0.02 above the baseline, so code explains itself.
A release may not be pushed while the last whole-suite run has a failing test.
Line coverage from the last whole-suite run may not drop more than half a point below its baseline.

args: -- awk -v t="$(stat -c %Y storage/coverage/clover.xml 2>/dev/null)" 'BEGIN { if (t == "") exit 1; printf "%d\n", (systime() - t) / 86400 }'
why: The whole-suite reports may be at most seven days old, so tests-failing and coverage read a recent run.
The last whole-suite run may not log a lazily loaded relation beyond the baseline, so N+1 queries are caught before release.
The mutation score may not drop more than one point below its baseline, so the tests keep catching changed behaviour.

args: runner=quality/bin/in-server.sh metric=failed junit=storage/coverage/junit.xml reset=storage/logs/lazy-loading.log bin=env -- XDEBUG_MODE=coverage vendor/bin/phpunit --coverage-html storage/coverage/html --coverage-clover storage/coverage/clover.xml --coverage-xml storage/coverage/coverage-xml --log-junit storage/coverage/junit.xml --coverage-text
why: The whole suite may not fail on a baseline run, and it writes the coverage and test reports the release rows read.
